all.title: Read-scope Mission sessions with Claude Read or Codex shell are device-approvable
all.attack: F-01 refuses only write-scoped provider sessions. A read-scope Mission whose routed child is claude (--tools Read, restricted) or codex (--sandbox read-only, which still runs a shell) passes deviceMissionRefusal and can be approved from the phone. all.title: Device mission.start launches a ready write-scoped Mission with no device re-check
all.attack: A workstation approves a write-scoped Mission with start:false, leaving it in state ready. The phone calls mission.start. missionCommand checks only state==='ready' and that the Mission is not Agent-owned. all.title: Replanned Mission cannot be started from a stale ready state

all.title: Device answers to provider.execute requests cannot launch tool-capable children
all.attack: Device calls mission.respond on a provider.execute request for a write or non-ollama child (allow_once or allow_batch) to launch that child. Also checks whether allow_batch on provider.execute can bypass the tasks.approve launch.
all.blockedBy: deviceRequestRefusal (~1952-1960) returns APPROVAL_ON_HOST unless the child task is deviceMayLaunch (ollama, not a remote tag). respond() calls deviceRequestRefusal for non-deny decisions (~3200-3204). verdicts.reasoning:
The claimed chain holds against the code as read (read-only, no tests run).

Confirmed pieces:
- http.server.ts approve device branch (~552-563) checks only the pre-launch task: `pending.provider` must pass `deviceMayLaunch` (provider ollama, not a remote tag). It then calls `manager.approve(id, actor)` with no further device check.
- manager.server.ts approve(id, by) (~964) passes only the approval kind to launch(); `by` is used only to emit an event after launch. launch() takes no actor, so nothing downstream can apply the device rule.
- launch() ~1040 checks eligibility on preProvider (availability only). ~1054 runs revalidateCandidate; on failure, for non-manual routing (routingMode is auto when no override is set, and http.server.ts ~57-60 defaults undefined/auto to auto), it calls rerouteFromDecision (~1067) and rewrites task.provider via this.update. ~1094 re-reads provider from the db. No deviceMayLaunch or actor check exists in manager.server.ts (grep finds none).
- routing.server.ts preLaunchRevalidate (~324-332): for DISCOVERED_MODEL, if the registry has facts and the model is not listed, it returns ok:false, so the reroute trigger is real. The precondition is Host-side (model unlisted while the provider stays ready), which matches the finding's own stated precondition.
- rerouteFromDecision walks record.fallback_order, built as selection.order from eligible candidates (safeDecisionRecord ~542). hardExclusions (~190) only enforces tools when requirements.needs_tools is set, so a plain text chat keeps claude/codex as eligible fallback entries. rerouteFromDecision applies only preLaunchRevalidate and codexCompatibilityFresh, with no tool filter and no device filter.
- claudeLaunchArgs (adapters.server.ts ~403-408): with no executionScope (direct tasks have none) it grants Read,Write,Edit,Bash,PowerShell on win32, with acceptEdits and no prompts.
- Commit b345aa3's message says DEV-01 direct-task launches are approved on the Windows Host, so the reroute path defeats an intended guarantee.

I found no blocking code. The one mitigating factor is that the trigger needs a Host-side model-list change between submit and approve, which the device cannot force. That narrows likelihood, not the violation, so I kept HIGH. Note the claim's line reference (1053) is close to the actual preflight at 1054, and the cited files are real.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: Thread the approving actor into launch() (manager.approve already has `by`). After the reroute, and before the provider is re-read and spawned, refuse when the actor is a device and the final provider/model fails deviceMayLaunch. Better, filter rerouteFromDecision candidates by deviceMayLaunch when the approving actor is a device. Also add a launch-time deviceMayLaunch check on the final `provider`/`model` so no path that rewrites provider can bypass the device rule.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not find blocking code. The chain holds as described:

1. Device approve gate (http.server.ts:552-569) checks only the pre-launch task: non-mission, and deviceMayLaunch(pending) (device-authority.server.ts:29-31). It runs before manager.approve and never re-checks after a reroute.
2. launch() (manager.server.ts:1038-1041) only checks availability via eligibility(), so a model removed from the listing still passes.
3. At manager.server.ts:1053-1067 a failed revalidateCandidate reroutes for AUTO tasks. preLaunchRevalidate (routing.server.ts:324-332) fails for DISCOVERED_MODEL when the model is no longer listed or snapshotted, and the facts.length guard does not apply when facts exist.
4. rerouteFromDecision (manager.server.ts:546-606) walks record.fallback_order with only the constraints, no device or tool-free filter. Claude and Codex enter fallback_order when needs_tools is false (routing.server.ts:191; router-requirements.ts:95 sets needs_tools only for coding, tool_execution and verification classes). A plain chat is therefore eligible for them.
5. The reroute persists the new provider via update() (manager.server.ts:1079-1095). update() enforces only executionScope and mission immutability, and both are undefined for direct tasks. The adapter task is built from the rerouted record (manager.server.ts:1111-1134, 1305-1327), and the adapter is re-looked-up from the re-read provider (line 1106-1107).
6. claudeLaunchArgs (adapters.server.ts:403-409) with executionScope undefined grants Read,Write,Edit,Bash,PowerShell.

The contract at test-results/ma3/t9/remote-command-contract.md:56 lists "a direct-task approve of a tool-capable or hosted route" as a refusal case, and no test in remote-remediation.test.ts or remote-device.test.ts covers the reroute path.

The Ollama model must become unlisted or unsnapshotted while the provider stays ready (a provider going offline is caught earlier at line 1040). The device cannot force it, so practical likelihood is lower than the raw authority break suggests. I kept HIGH because the invariant break is direct and unscoped Bash/PowerShell on the workstation is reachable from a phone approve without any other signal.

Alternatively, refuse any device-originated revalidation failure with "Route again" instead of rerouting. Add a regression test in remote-remediation.test.ts that removes the Ollama model between submit and approve and asserts the device approve is refused, not rerouted to claude or codex.

verdicts.reasoning:
The core mechanical claim is confirmed. deviceMissionRefusal (manager.server.ts:1962-1976) refuses only providers.sessions.steps[].scope.access === "write" (line 1970). A read-scope plan has risks READ plus EXECUTE (authorization.server.ts:44, 72), and neither EXECUTE nor filesystem.read/list/exists is in WORKSTATION_ONLY_RISKS or sensitive/hardApproval (local.server.ts:36-38 marks them READ with no flag), so the function returns null and mission.approve proceeds. Routing to claude or codex for read steps is plausible: launchModel's requiresFilesystem (manager.server.ts:1258-1261) is true for non-localOnly steps. Once approved, approveDelegated runs without a provider.execute ask whenever taskViolation returns null (manager.server.ts:1357-1395), so the per-launch device gate in deviceRequestRefusal (line 1952-1957) is never reached for such children.

No concrete blocking code exists, so refuted=false. Severity is downgraded to LOW for these reasons:
- The commit and the docs treat read sessions as a bounded authority. docs/MA0_ARCHITECTURE.md:99 says "Codex read uses its read-only sandbox; Claude read exposes only its Read tool", and docs/MA0_SECURITY_MODEL.md:55 describes the read-only argv. Read-scope Missions are a deliberate, Host-approved level.
- The contract (test-results/ma3/t9/remote-command-contract.md section 2) never mentions read sessions, so the phone gate for them is an unresolved owner-intent question, not a stated rule that is violated. The contract's item 3 (provider.execute asks) is the closest rule, and it fires only on asks, not auto-launch.
- The Claude path-escape concern (absolute Read path outside the approved roots) is not device-specific. The workstation owner could approve the same plan, so it is a Host confinement question rather than a phone-authority bypass. I could not verify the claude CLI's runtime path restriction from source, so that part stays unconfirmed.
- The finding's line 1968 is the comment; the actual check is line 1970. Immaterial.

Recommended action: treat as an owner-intent decision. If the owner wants parity with DEV-01 (device may approve only local tool-free routes), extend the refusal to any providers.execution plan whose sessions include a claude or codex route, or require the Host to route read sessions locally.

Option B (keep as designed): document in remote-command-contract.md section 2 that read-scope Mission sessions (codex read-only sandbox, claude Read) are approvable by a paired device, and add a test pinning that decision. Separately, confirm the claude CLI's runtime path restriction for --restricted Read, since that is a Host confinement question that applies to the workstation too.

The cited mechanics hold. deviceMissionRefusal (manager.server.ts ~1968-1971) refuses only step.scope.access === "write", so a read-scope Mission with provider sessions is not refused by that check. launchModel (~1258-1261) routes non-local read steps to a filesystem-capable provider, and codexLaunchArgs (adapters.server.ts ~392-400) keeps the shell under the read-only sandbox. claudeLaunchArgs (~403-409) gives Claude only the Read tool, with no path restriction. Nothing in the code blocks the claim, so refuted=false.

It is still not a clear defect, for three reasons. (1) The author encoded this as intended: remote-remediation.test.ts lines 197-208 assert readView.remote.answerable === true ("a read-only provider session stays answerable remotely") and that the device approval returns 200. (2) remote-command-contract.md section 2 does not mention read sessions, so the contract neither forbids nor requires this. all.title: Failed device-approved Mission keeps a live envelope and Retry revives it
all.attack: Device D approves plain Mission M (envelope E, grantedBy device:D). M reaches state 'failed' (a step fails; failMission in manager.server.ts sets state=failed and never clears authorizationId). Workstation revokes D. endDeviceGrants iterates only missionsIn(MISSION_ACTIVE) = ready/running/waiting_for_user/verifying, so M (failed) is skipped and E.revokedAt stays null. Workstation later calls mission.retry on M: retry() (manager.server.ts ~3455) only refuses when envelope.revokedAt or expired, so it re-arms M to ready and start()s it under E, which is still the revoked device's grant. Precondition: M has at least one failed step (retry's own precondition). Not reachable by the device itself (mission.retry is not in REMOTE), so it needs a workstation Retry, but the stated contract is that a lost device's authority ends with revocation.
all.evidence: http.server.ts loop: `for (const mission of missions.store.missionsIn(MISSION_ACTIVE))` then `if (!envelope || envelope.revokedAt || envelope.grantedBy !== deviceActor) continue;`. manager.server.ts retry(): `if (!envelope || envelope.revokedAt || envelope.expiresAt <= Date.now()) throw ...`; `if (mission.state === "failed") mission = this.setMission(mission, { state: "ready" ...})`; `if (mission.state === "ready") mission = this.start(mission);`. machine.ts MISSION_ACTIVE excludes 'failed'; failed:['ready','planning','stopped'] allows retry. remote-remediation.test.ts asserts revocation only for the stopped (running/ready) case.

all.title: Sequential revocation loop: one hung stop blocks revoking later Missions
all.attack: The approvals loop awaits missions.stop() per mission. stop() awaits bus.cancel(), which awaits settling promises of in-flight capability runs. A settle promise resolves only in the finally of the run after adapter.execute returns (bus.server.ts:303); the abort timer (bus.server.ts:267) only signals and does not force settle. If an adapter ignores abort, mission #1's stop never resolves, so the loop never reaches mission #2 and its envelope stays live. Mission #2 keeps admitting capability runs and child tasks under a grant from the revoked device until its own envelope expiry. Fix direction: revoke all matching envelopes synchronously in one pass before awaiting any stop.
all.evidence: bus.server.ts:265 `this.settling.set(base.id, new Promise(...))`; :267 setTimeout only calls controller.abort; :303 `finally { ...; settled(); }`. bus.cancel: `await Promise.all(settling)`. http.server.ts endDeviceGrants: `await missions.stop(mission.id, ...)` inside the for-of over a pre-fetched array.

all.title: Errors swallowed after revocation leave a Mission active and unstopped with no audit event
all.attack: Revocation writes revokedAt first, then calls stop() inside try/catch that silently ignores every error. (a) If saveAuthorization throws, nothing is revoked, approvals is not incremented, and the envelope stays live with no event. (b) If stop() throws after the revoke (manager.server.ts stop() has a try/finally with no catch, so an exception from cancelChildren/bus.cancel or a store write propagates), the mission is not set to 'stopped'. Revocation still blocks new launches, but already-running child tasks may survive because cancelChildren calls bus.cancel before the task-stop loop. The device.revoked event still reports these Missions as 'Mission approval(s) ... ended', which is inaccurate. Only a workstation Stop recovers the mission.
all.evidence: http.server.ts: `try { ... missions.store.saveAuthorization({ ...envelope, revokedAt: Date.now() }); approvals++; await missions.stop(...) } catch { /* Already ending ... */ }`. manager.server.ts stop(): `try { ... await this.cancelChildren(...) ... return this.view(stopped); } finally { this.stopping.delete(id); }`. cancelChildren: `await this.bus.cancel({ missionId }); for (const step ...) tasks.stop(...)`.

all.title: Active Mission states are all covered; new launches blocked after revoke
all.attack: Can a revoked device's approved Mission keep running via ready, running, waiting_for_user or verifying?
all.evidence: All four states are in MISSION_ACTIVE and get stop(): stop() accepts ready/running/waiting_for_user/verifying per machine.ts. Child-task launch re-checks taskViolation, which returns 'authorization revoked' when envelope.revokedAt is set (authorization.server.ts:268), and the launch path has no await between that check and tasks.approveDelegated (manager.server.ts ~1357-1391). Capability requests call decide(), which denies on revokedAt (authorization.server.ts:174). Running child tasks are stopped by cancelChildren; capability runs are aborted via bus.cancel (cancelledMissions set).
all.blockedBy: MISSION_ACTIVE loop + stop() + taskViolation revokedAt check (authorization.server.ts:268) + decide revokedAt deny (authorization.server.ts:174) + cancelChildren

all.title: Revoke-then-stop ordering does not break stop()
all.attack: Does revoking the envelope before stop() break stop(), since stop may need the envelope?
all.evidence: stop() reads the Mission and agentic delegation only; it never reads the envelope for control flow (the view() it returns includes envelope as a plain field). The revoke and this.stopping.add(id) run synchronously before stop's first await, so no admission can interleave between them.
all.blockedBy: stop() does not gate on authorization; synchronous ordering in the loop

all.title: No race between device approval and revocation, or with in-flight admission
all.attack: Could a device approve a Mission after revocation, or could an in-flight launch or capability run escape cancellation?
all.evidence: Device commands revalidate with authenticateDevice at http.server.ts:459-461, and missionCommand reaches mission.approve with no await in between (lines 461-532), so approve is atomic relative to the revoke UPDATE. Capability bus non-batch path has no await between decision (bus.server.ts:188) and inFlight.set (:263). The batch path has one await, after which it re-reads cancellation, mission state and envelope (bus.server.ts:199-200) and re-decides against the fresh envelope. Task launch has no await between check and approveDelegated.
all.blockedBy: Synchronous device revalidation before approve; no await windows in capability/task admission; post-await re-check in batch path

all.title: Agent Missions are excluded from the plain-Mission revocation loop correctly
all.attack: Could an Agent Mission be wrongly stopped or left running by the plain-Mission loop?
all.evidence: The loop skips `missions.agentic.exists(mission.id) || mission.origin.startsWith("agent:")`, the same predicate as deviceMissionRefusal (manager.server.ts ~1963). Agent Missions can never receive a device-granted envelope because approve() refuses device actors on them before any state change (manager.server.ts:719-721). Agent consent by a device is handled by the agentic loop keyed on authorization_provenance.actor.
all.blockedBy: deviceMissionRefusal runs before approval; agentic loop covers Agent consent

all.title: envelope.grantedBy format matches the revocation key
all.attack: Does envelope.grantedBy match the device:<id> key the revocation compares against?
all.evidence: actorOf(principal) returns `device:${principal.id}` (device-authority.server.ts:116-117); that value is passed as access.actor into missionCommand (http.server.ts:532) and then as `by` into approve(), which writes grantedBy. device.revoke uses `device:${id}` with the same device row id. The equality is pinned by remote-remediation.test.ts:253-254.
all.blockedBy: Consistent actorOf/device:<id> derivation

all.title: Expired or idle devices are not revoked, so their Mission approvals survive
all.attack: A phone whose session expires or goes idle (deviceStillValid/authenticateDevice fail) is not an explicit revocation, so endDeviceGrants never runs and its envelopes stay live until their own expiry. The device itself cannot act, but a Mission it approved keeps running on its own.
all.evidence: endDeviceGrants is called only from the device.revoke branch when `local` is true (http.server.ts ~ device.revoke). Self sign-out also keeps approvals by design (remote-remediation.test.ts:265). This matches the documented sign-out behavior, so it is a gap only if expiry should be treated as loss.

all.title: No device approval path bypasses the planReference requirement
all.attack: Can a device get an envelope for a plain Mission without a plan via another path?
all.evidence: Of REMOTE actions, only mission.approve creates an envelope. mission.start requires state 'ready' (commands.server.ts:56) and creates no envelope. The Agent path (agent-runtime.server.ts:168 calls missions.approve with the actor) is refused for device actors at manager.server.ts:720 before the plan check; agent.start is refused for devices at agent-runtime.server.ts:868. mission.respond creates batches under an existing envelope only. mission.replan is workstation-only.
all.blockedBy: REMOTE allowlist; start requires ready; Agent refusal precedes plan check

all.title: plan cannot be supplied as non-string or empty to bypass
all.attack: Can plan be a non-string, empty, whitespace, or oversized value that is treated as absent or matches?
all.evidence: commands.server.ts:52 passes `data.plan === undefined ? undefined : text(data.plan, 200)`. text() (line 12) throws CommandRefusedError for non-strings, empty or whitespace-only strings, and length >200. null, numbers, arrays and objects are refused, not treated as undefined. Any string that is not the current digest is refused at manager.server.ts:717. Only an explicit undefined reaches the device refusal at line 723, which then refuses.
all.blockedBy: text() validation + digest equality check (manager.server.ts:717) + undefined refusal (manager.server.ts:723)

all.title: planReference is available to a legitimate client for every non-agentic waiting_for_approval Mission
all.attack: Is planReference computed for non-agentic Missions so a legitimate phone can always satisfy the check?
all.evidence: remoteVerdicts (manager.server.ts ~1999-2010) sets planReference = agenticPlanReference(mission.id) for every mission in state waiting_for_approval, with no agentic condition. It is applied to every snapshot via http.server.ts:338, and deviceSnapshot spreads the snapshot so missions are kept. hostPathFree leaves the hex sha256 digest unchanged (no drive letter, slash or path prefix).

all.title: Phone sends plan only when its local row carries planReference; otherwise fails closed
all.attack: Does the phone always send plan on approve?
all.evidence: use-island.ts:762-763 reads planReference from the local mission row and sends `...(plan ? { plan } : {})` with no state check. Rows come from snapshot.missions (use-island.ts:443). If the row lacks planReference (stale or non-waiting state), the approve is sent without plan and the Host refuses it (manager.server.ts:723-724). This is fail-closed, not a bypass; the risk is only that approval becomes impossible from a stale view. I did not verify the mission.tsx approve-button condition.

all.title: No time-of-check/time-of-use gap between reviewed plan and envelope
all.attack: Could a replan or plan change between the device's reviewed planReference and the envelope creation?
all.evidence: approve() is synchronous from the planReference compare (717) through envelope creation and saveAuthorization. replan() (~line 3500-3540) requires non-running steps and nulls authorizationId, and plan changes alter steps, so the digest changes and the compare fails. The digest covers step id, executor, scope, verification and requiredCapabilities.
all.blockedBy: Synchronous approve; digest over steps changes on replan

all.title: planReference does not directly digest requestedScope; no unbound mutation found
all.attack: Could requestedScope (budget, riskClasses, capabilities, providers) change while the digest stays equal, so the device approves a scope it did not review?

So with the current code, scope cannot change without the steps digest changing. This is a defense-in-depth gap, not a current bypass.
all.blockedBy: requestedScope is derived deterministically from steps and create-time constants; no mutation path found

verified.title: Failed device-approved Mission keeps a live envelope and Retry revives it
verified.attack: Device D approves plain Mission M (envelope E, grantedBy device:D). M reaches state 'failed' (a step fails; failMission in manager.server.ts sets state=failed and never clears authorizationId). Workstation revokes D. endDeviceGrants iterates only missionsIn(MISSION_ACTIVE) = ready/running/waiting_for_user/verifying, so M (failed) is skipped and E.revokedAt stays null. Workstation later calls mission.retry on M: retry() (manager.server.ts ~3455) only refuses when envelope.revokedAt or expired, so it re-arms M to ready and start()s it under E, which is still the revoked device's grant. Precondition: M has at least one failed step (retry's own precondition). Not reachable by the device itself (mission.retry is not in REMOTE), so it needs a workstation Retry, but the stated contract is that a lost device's authority ends with revocation.
verified.evidence: http.server.ts loop: `for (const mission of missions.store.missionsIn(MISSION_ACTIVE))` then `if (!envelope || envelope.revokedAt || envelope.grantedBy !== deviceActor) continue;`. manager.server.ts retry(): `if (!envelope || envelope.revokedAt || envelope.expiresAt <= Date.now()) throw ...`; `if (mission.state === "failed") mission = this.setMission(mission, { state: "ready" ...})`; `if (mission.state === "ready") mission = this.start(mission);`. machine.ts MISSION_ACTIVE excludes 'failed'; failed:['ready','planning','stopped'] allows retry. remote-remediation.test.ts asserts revocation only for the stopped (running/ready) case.

verdicts.reasoning:
Could not refute F02-1; the code matches the claim on every link.

1. http.server.ts:849-856 (endDeviceGrants, commit b345aa3) iterates only `missions.store.missionsIn(MISSION_ACTIVE)`. MISSION_ACTIVE in machine.ts:30 is ready/running/waiting_for_user/verifying, so a `failed` Mission is skipped and its envelope is never revoked.
2. manager.server.ts failMission (971-992) sets state=failed and calls workspace.releaseMission, but never revokes or clears the envelope. authorizationId stays set and the envelope keeps revokedAt=null.
3. manager.server.ts retry (3447-3500) only refuses when the envelope is missing, revoked, or expired (3455). It then sets failed to ready and calls start(), which schedules tick(). tick (~855-880) checks only that the envelope exists, its runtime budget, and the mission pause/stop gates. It never checks grantedBy or whether the granting device is still paired, so the revived run executes under the revoked device's grant until expiresAt.
4. Reachability: commands.server.ts:17 and :62 expose mission.retry through missionCommand, which rejects non-local, non-REMOTE actions (line 30). mission.retry is not in REMOTE, so a device cannot reach it. A workstation caller (src/store/use-island.ts:791) can.

Mitigating factors that keep this at MEDIUM and not higher: the trigger is a deliberate workstation Retry by the owner, not a device action, and the envelope still expires on its normal expiresAt. The stated contract (commit message: "revokes and stops the plain Missions that device approved") implies that a lost device's authority should end on revocation, and this path leaves a live envelope that the owner's Retry revives without any indication it is device-granted.

Suggested fix (not applied): in endDeviceGrants, scan all missions with a non-null authorizationId in any non-terminal state including failed and waiting_for_user, or query authorizations by grantedBy, and revoke their envelopes. Optionally also refuse retry() when the envelope's grantedBy is a revoked device actor.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: In http.server.ts endDeviceGrants, widen the plain-Mission scan beyond MISSION_ACTIVE so that failed (and waiting_for_user) Missions whose envelope has grantedBy === deviceActor and revokedAt === null also get their envelope revoked (the stop call can stay limited to active ones). Alternatively, query the authorization rows by grantedBy directly. Optionally add a guard in manager.server.ts retry() that refuses when the envelope's grantedBy is a revoked device. Add a test that revokes a device after a plain Mission has failed, then asserts retry is refused.

verdicts.reasoning: Tried to refute F02-1 and found no blocking code. (1) endDeviceGrants (http.server.ts:850-854) iterates only missionsIn(MISSION_ACTIVE), and machine.ts:30 defines MISSION_ACTIVE as ready/running/waiting_for_user/verifying, so a failed Mission is skipped and its envelope is never saved with revokedAt. (2) manager.server.ts failMission (~971-993) sets state=failed and does not clear authorizationId or revoke the envelope, so the device-granted envelope stays live. (3) retry() (manager.server.ts:3447-3497) checks only envelope.revokedAt and expiresAt before re-arming a failed Mission to ready and calling start(); nothing checks grantedBy or the device's current revocation status. (4) Device cannot reach this path directly: mission.retry is not in REMOTE (commands.server.ts:27), so a device gets WorkstationRequiredError. mission.start requires state ready (commands.server.ts:56), and approve requires waiting_for_approval, so neither gives a device a revival path. (5) mission.replan on failed (manager.server.ts:3506, 3515-3518) does revoke the old envelope, but replan is workstation-only and is not the retry path. The only real bound is envelope expiry, which the finding already acknowledges, so the gap is real but operator-triggered and time-bounded. MEDIUM stands, and the remediation test only covers the running/ready stop case as the finding says.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: In endDeviceGrants (http.server.ts ~850), widen the Mission scan beyond MISSION_ACTIVE to include failed and waiting_for_user (or all non-terminal states that can reach retry), so the device-granted envelope is revoked before the stop. Alternatively, have manager.server.ts failMission or retry() refuse to re-arm when the envelope's grantedBy is a revoked device. Add a remediation test for a failed device-approved plain Mission: revoke the device, then assert the envelope is revoked and mission.retry throws.

all.title: Base64, digests and URL schemes are not false positives

all.title: No performance or ReDoS problem on large inputs
all.attack: Large or adversarial strings cause catastrophic regex backtracking or slow snapshot delivery.
all.evidence: Measured on Node v24 via probe: 5 MB plain string 6.5 ms; ~2.6 MB path-dense string 1.7 ms; 500k-backslash run 0.4 ms; 500k-slash run 1.4 ms; 'C:\\' + 500k 'a ' 0.8 ms; 2000-object snapshot 1.9 ms. All regexes are linear (no nested quantifiers). Cost is a full deep copy per /state call and per SSE event batch (up to 500 events).
all.blockedBy: Linear regexes; measured timings well under budget.

verified.title: Embedded Windows paths with spaces leak their tail (folder and file names)
verified.attack: A device-visible string contains C:\Users\owner\My Projects\secret.txt (or the same path in forward-slash or JSON-escaped form). Only the first space-delimited fragment is removed.
verified.evidence: Probe output: 'result in C:\Users\owner\My Projects\secret.txt' => 'result in [Host path] Projects\secret.txt'; 'in C:/Users/owner/My Projects/x' => 'in [Host path] Projects/x'; JSON-encoded {"p":"C:\\Users\\owner\\My Projects\\x"} => '{"p":"[Host path] Projects[Host path]"}' (fragment kept); 'He said "C:\Users\owner\My Projects\x y"' => '...[Host path] Projects\x y...'. Cause: the embedded regexes stop at whitespace, and WHOLE_HOST_PATH only fires at string start. The existing test (remote-remediation.test.ts:275) uses 'project-a' with no space, so this is untested.
verified.failure_scenario: A paired phone shows text containing a Host folder name with a space and the file name after it, for example 'Projects\secret.txt'. The T-01 invariant (no Host folder facts to a device) is violated for any path whose folder name contains a space, which is common (Program Files, My Documents, Client Work).

verdicts.reasoning: Claim confirmed by reading the code and by running the same regex chain (copied verbatim from hostPathFree, device-authority.server.ts lines 435-437) as a standalone node script. Embedded drive-letter and forward-slash paths stop at the first space, and the leading-anchored WHOLE_HOST_PATH check only applies when the whole string starts with a path. Observed outputs: "result in C:\Users\owner\My Projects\secret.txt" => "result in [Host path] Projects\secret.txt"; "in C:/Users/owner/My Projects/x" => "in [Host path] Projects/x"; "see \"C:\Users\owner\My Projects\x y\"" => "see \"[Host path] Projects\x y\"". hostPathFree is applied to every device-bound payload (http.server.ts lines 369, 444, 780, 803), so any embedded path with a space in its folder name leaks the folder tail and file name to a paired device, contrary to the T-01 invariant. The existing test (remote-remediation.test.ts:274-275) covers only whole-string paths and a space-free embedded path, so the gap is untested. No blocking code found: the scrub is applied to these strings, and nothing else redacts them first. Severity is MEDIUM rather than higher because only a fragment (folder tail plus filename) leaks and only when a device-visible string embeds a spaced path.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: In hostPathFree (and hidePaths for consistency), make the embedded drive-letter and forward-slash patterns consume spaces up to a path terminator instead of stopping at whitespace, e.g. replace the `[^\s'"`,;)]*` tail with a pattern that allows spaces (`[^'"`,;)\r\n]*`, or a segment-based pattern such as `(?:[^\\/\s'"`,;)]+[\\/])*[^\\/\s'"`,;)]*` with spaces allowed inside segments). Accept over-redaction of trailing words in exchange for no fragment leak. Add tests for `result in C:\Users\owner\My Projects\secret.txt`, `in C:/Users/owner/My Projects/x`, and a JSON-escaped path with a space in remote-remediation.test.ts next to line 275.

verdicts.reasoning: Not refuted. I extracted the actual hostPathFree source (device-authority.server.ts lines 425-443) to a scratchpad file and ran it with node --experimental-strip-types, without importing anything from the repo. Results: "result in C:\Users\owner\My Projects\secret.txt" becomes "result in [Host path] Projects\secret.txt"; "in C:/Users/owner/My Projects/x" becomes "in [Host path] Projects/x"; the JSON-escaped {"p":"C:\\Users\\owner\\My Projects\\x"} becomes {"p":"[Host path] Projects[Host path]"}. The finding's probe results reproduce exactly. The embedded drive-letter regex (line 435) and the UNC and POSIX regexes all use [^\s'"`,;)]*, so they stop at the first space. WHOLE_HOST_PATH (line 425) only fires when the path starts the string. No other scrub runs after hostPathFree on the device branches: http.server.ts lines 369, 444, 780 and 803 all route through it, so nothing blocks the leak on those surfaces. The existing test at remote-remediation.test.ts:274-275 covers only a whole path with spaces and a path with no space, so the gap is untested. Severity stays MEDIUM, not higher: the leak exposes a folder-name fragment and file name rather than the full absolute path, and it needs a device-visible string that contains a Host path with a space, which I did not confirm is reachable in a real flow. I did not edit any repo file, run npm test, or start a Host.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: In hostPathFree (and hidePaths), make the embedded drive-letter, UNC and POSIX patterns consume to the end of the path rather than the first whitespace. For example, stop at a quote, backtick, comma, semicolon, closing paren, newline, or a run of two or more spaces, or at the end of the string. Add a regression case to remote-remediation.test.ts near line 275, e.g. hostPathFree("result in C:\\Users\\owner\\My Projects\\secret.txt") must not contain "Projects", and cover the JSON-escaped and forward-slash forms.

verified.title: Node fs error text from project.artifact reaches the device with path tail
verified.attack: Device calls project.artifact for a verified artifact whose file under a Project folder is missing or unreadable. Node's error message contains the full Host path, which hidePaths (weaker) scrubs before the CommandRefusedError path.
verified.evidence: project-service.server.ts:286 runs statSync(path) with no try/catch, so a missing file throws "ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'C:\...\My Projects\repo\report.md'". http.server.ts:538-540 wraps project.* errors as CommandRefusedError(device ? hidePaths(message) : message). Probe pipeline: hidePaths then hostPathFree gives "ENOENT ... open '[Host path] Projects\bun-router\secret.txt'" and "EACCES ... scandir '[Host path] Files\Owner Notes\x'" (for 'C:\Program Files\Owner Notes\x'). Note: registry.refresh (project-registry.server.ts:361-375) swallows verify errors, so project.get does not throw these; the reachable case is project.artifact.
verified.failure_scenario: Paired phone requests project.artifact for an artifact whose file was deleted from C:\Users\<user>\My Projects\<repo>\. The refusal text returned to the device is "...stat '[Host path] Projects\<repo>\report.md'", revealing a folder name fragment and a file name.

verdicts.reasoning:
Not refuted. The chain holds in the current code:
1. project-service.server.ts:278-289: for a file-backed artifact, the only check before the read is registry.verify(project), which validates the project folder identity only (project-registry.server.ts:341-344). statSync(path) at line 286 has no try/catch, so a deleted artifact file throws Node's ENOENT with the full path in the message.
2. DEVICE_RIGHTS maps project.artifact to "read" (device-authority.server.ts:56), so a paired device can reach this path.
3. http.server.ts:533-540: the project.* error is rethrown as CommandRefusedError(hidePaths(message)) for a device.
4. http.server.ts:798-804: the outer catch applies hostPathFree(safeError(...).message) for a device before json().
Running the copied pure functions on "ENOENT: ... stat 'C:\Users\allam\My Projects\repo\report.md'" gives "ENOENT: ... stat '[Host path] Projects\repo\report.md'" after both passes. The tail is sent to the device. Paths without spaces are fully scrubbed, so the leak needs a space in the path, which is common (My Projects, Program Files).
Correction to the finding's mechanism: hostPathFree also stops at whitespace, so it would leak the same tail on the raw message. The defect is the whitespace-terminated scrub in both functions, not only the weaker hidePaths step. The existing test (remote-remediation.test.ts:274) covers only whole-value paths with spaces, not embedded ones.
Severity is kept at MEDIUM because the device-path invariant ("local folder paths never reach a paired device") is explicit and tested, and the leak exposes a folder fragment and a file name. The trigger is narrow: the artifact file must be deleted after verification.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: Scrub embedded Windows and POSIX paths up to the closing quote or terminator, not the first whitespace, in both hidePaths and hostPathFree (e.g., match a drive path with a lazy or quote-bounded pattern such as /[A-Za-z]:\\[^'"`\n]*/ when inside quotes). Alternatively, in the device branch of the catch at http.server.ts:540 and 803, replace any refusal text that still contains a path-like fragment with a generic message. Add a regression test in remote-remediation.test.ts asserting that hostPathFree("ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'C:\\Users\\u\\My Projects\\repo\\report.md'") contains no 'Projects' or 'report.md' fragment.

verdicts.reasoning:
Finding T01-12 is not refuted. The leak path is reachable and the scrubbing pipeline does not remove the tail.

Reachability:
- project-service.server.ts:280-289 (artifact()): for a file-backed artifact under the Project root, it calls this.registry.verify(project), which checks only root identity, then statSync(path) with no try/catch. A deleted or unreadable file throws a Node fs error whose message embeds the full path (ENOENT ... stat 'C:\...\report.md'). The hash check comes after, so the fs error is what surfaces.
- device-authority.server.ts:56: "project.artifact": "read" is in DEVICE_RIGHTS, so a paired device can call it. project-service.server.ts:56-57 dispatches it without a local-only gate.
- http.server.ts:533-541: the catch wraps the error as CommandRefusedError(device ? hidePaths(message) : message).
- http.server.ts:799-804: the outer handler applies hostPathFree(safeError(...).message) for device CommandRefusedError. This is the second scrub the claim describes.

Leak confirmed by running the regexes copied from device-authority.server.ts:419-438 on a sample message (scratch script only, no repo code run):
- raw: ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat 'C:\Users\allam\My Projects\repo\report.md'
- hidePaths: ... stat '[Host path] Projects\repo\report.md'
- final after hostPathFree: identical, since hostPathFree's drive-letter pattern no longer matches and the UNC and POSIX patterns do not apply.

So the device receives the project folder name fragment ("Projects\repo") and the artifact filename. The hidePaths drive-letter regex stops at whitespace, which is why the tail survives. The commit's stated invariant (no local folder facts reach a paired device) is violated.

Nothing blocks the path: no earlier guard rejects the request, and safeError only redacts secrets and control characters. The one qualifier is that the trigger requires a verified artifact whose file was removed or became unreadable after verification, so it is an edge-case leak of a path fragment and a filename, not a full path or file contents. MEDIUM is a fair rating.

Fix suggestion: have artifact() catch fs errors and rethrow a path-free message (for example using error.code only), or make the device branch scrub whole quoted fs paths including spaces before any other scrubbing.
verdicts.fixSuggestion: In project-service.server.ts artifact(), wrap the statSync/readFileSync calls (lines 286-289) in try/catch and rethrow a path-free Error (for example "Artifact file is unavailable." with the Node error code only). Alternatively, in device-authority.server.ts hidePaths/hostPathFree, scrub quoted or whole fs-error path arguments including spaces (for example matching from a drive letter up to the closing quote) so the "My Projects" tail is removed. Add a regression test in remote-remediation.test.ts with an ENOENT message containing a path with a space.

all.title: T-01 SSE read loop can break early and turn a slow first chunk into a false failure

This is loud, not vacuous, so it cannot pass wrongly; it is a flake risk. The raced read promise is also left pending and abandoned on break, which is harmless because controller.abort() rejects it inside the already-settled race.

Strengthen: wait for the first chunk with a longer per-read deadline (e.g. up to 5 s) and keep reading until an 'id:' line is seen or the overall deadline elapses, instead of breaking on a single 300 ms timeout.
